questions.question:
**Select the grammatically correct sentence.**

A. The Supriya is the best girl in the class.

B. Supriya is the best girl in the class.

C. Supriya is best girl in the class.

D. The Supriya is a best girl in the class.
questions.solution:
The grammatically correct sentence is: "**B. Supriya is the best girl in the class.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is "**Supriya**," and the verb "**is**" agrees with the singular subject.
 
• The phrase "**the best girl in the class**" serves as the predicate adjective. It describes a quality or characteristic of the subject, "**Supriya**."
 
• The use of the superlative adjective "**best**" indicates that among all the girls in the class, Supriya has the highest degree of the quality being described.
 
• The phrase "**in the class**" is a prepositional phrase that provides additional information about where Supriya's quality as the best girl applies.
 
• So, the sentence is **grammatically correct** because it follows the basic rules of English grammar and sentence structure.

Hence, **option 4** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: Incorrect due to the use of the article "**the**" before Supriya's name.
 
• Option 3: Incorrect due to the missing article "**the**" before "**best girl**."
 
• Option 4: Incorrect due to the use of the article "**a**" instead of "**the**" before "**best girl**."

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence In active voice.**

Pudding had already been prepared by her.
questions.solution:
The correct active voice is: **She had already prepared pudding.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is written in the passive voice.
 
• To convert this sentence to active voice, we need to make the subject of the sentence the doer of the action.
 
• Identify the subject, verb, and object:
 
 
• **Subject**: Pudding
 
• **Verb**: had been prepared
 
• **Object**: by her
 
 
 
• Determine the doer of the action (agent):
 
 
• The doer of the action is "**her**."
 
 
 
• Construct the active voice sentence:
 
 
• **Subject**: She (the doer of the action)
 
• **Verb**: had already prepared
 
• **Object**: pudding
 
 
 
• So, the active voice sentence is: *"**She had already prepared pudding.**"*

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**She has already prepared pudding**" is in the present perfect tense and is not in active voice.
 
• "**She have already prepared pudding**" is grammatically incorrect as the subject "she" requires the singular verb "has" or "had."
 
• "**She will prepare pudding**" is in the future tense and is not in an active voice.

questions.question: **Describe how you will tell your parents that Darshana was laughed at by all her classmates in active voice. **

options.text: All her classmates laughed at Darshana.
All her classmates laughing at Darshana.
Darshana is laughed at by all her classmates.
All her classmates will been laugh at Darshana.

questions.solution:
The correct active voice is: **All her classmates laughed at Darshana. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the past tense as the action happened in the past.
 
• To make a sentence from passive to active we need to follow the rules:
 
 
• Identify the Subject and Object.
 
• Reorder the Sentence.
 
• Select the Appropriate Verb.
 
 
 
• In the original sentence, "**Darshana**" is the subject, and "**by all her classmates**" indicates who performed the action.
 
• "**Laughed at**" is the verb phrase, and "**by all her classmates**" clarifies the action's doer.
 
• In active voice, the doer of the action comes before the action itself. So, we need to reorder the sentence to make the subject perform the action.
 
• In this case, the verb "**laughed**" remains the same.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2: "**All her classmates laughing at Darshana**" is in the present continuous tense and doesn't convey the past action.
 
• Option 3: "**Darshana is laughed at by all her classmates**" is in passive voice and doesn't clearly state who performed the action.
 
• Option 4: "**All her classmates will been laugh at Darshana**" has grammatical errors and doesn't convey the past action.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. “Well, you can’t make me”, she said, looking back at me.

B. She went on, “Well, you might try”, I responded, and she laughed.

C. She came in and we said hello, then she just looked at me and said, “What do you want?” McKechnie remembered.

D. “Well, I want you to grin and seem pleased”, I added.
questions.solution:
The correct sequence is: **CDAB**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let us look at the correct order of the sentences.
 
• Sentence **C **sets the context of the conversation and introduces the speaker.
 
• Sentence **D **is the response of the speaker to the question asked in sentence C.
 
• Sentence **A **shows a playful banter between the two speakers.
 
• Sentence **B **is a concluding statement made by one of the speakers.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Corrected sequence:** ***C**. She came in and we said hello, then she just looked at me and said, “What do you want?” McKechnie remembered. **D**. “Well, I want you to grin and seem pleased”, I added. **A**. “Well, you can’t make me”, she said, looking back at me. **B**. She went on, “Well, you might try”, I responded, and she laughed.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: (**ACBD**) has the first two sentences in the wrong order.
 
• Option 2: (**DCBA**) has the last two sentences in the wrong order.
 
• Option 3: (**BCDA**) has the first and last sentences in the wrong order.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. After examining these three approaches carefully I crossed the bridge and examined the Kedarnath pilgrim road for half a mile.

B. There were three approaches to the bridge; one from the north, one from the south and between these two a well-beaten footpath from the Rudraprayag bazaar.

C. Satisfied that the leopard had not crossed the river, I determined to put in operation my plan for closing the two bridges at night and thus confining the leopard to my side of the river.

D. Next, I examined the footpath on which three nights previously my goat had been killed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **BADC**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paragraph is about the author's search for a leopard that had been killing his goats.
 
• Sentence **B **introduces the setting and mentions the three approaches to the bridge.
 
• Sentence **A **follows up by describing the action taken after examining the approaches, where the speaker crosses the bridge and examines the Kedarnath pilgrim road.
 
• Sentence **D **provides further details about the footpath and the incident involving the speaker's goat being killed, adding to the narrative.
 
• Sentence **C **ties everything together, explaining the speaker's motivation and plan in response to their findings, which includes closing the bridges at night to confine the leopard to their side of the river.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**, i.e. '**BADC**'

**Correct order**: ***B**. There were three approaches to the bridge; one from the north, one from the south and between these two a well-beaten footpath from the Rudraprayag bazaar. **A**. After examining these three approaches carefully I crossed the bridge and examined the Kedarnath pilgrim road for half a mile. **D**. Next, I examined the footpath on which three nights previously my goat had been killed. **C**. Satisfied that the leopard had not crossed the river, I determined to put in operation my plan for closing the two bridges at night and thus confining the leopard to my side of the river.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DABC**: The order is incorrect as it starts with D, which should come after A and B.
 
• **CDAB**: The order is incorrect as it starts with C, which should come after A and B.
 
• **ABCD**: The order is incorrect as it starts with A, which should come after B.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.**

He was so curious __that he rose many questions__ in the meeting.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**that he raised many questions**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct verb form is '**raised**' and not '**rose**.'
 
• "**Rose**" is the past tense of the verb "**rise**" which means to move upwards, ascend, or increase in level or position.
 
• "**Raised**" is the past tense and past participle form of the verb "**raise**" which means to lift or elevate something, to bring up or present something for discussion, consideration, or attention.
 
• "**Was**" is used to describe a state of being or a condition in the past. 
 
• '**Many**' is used for countable nouns, hence '**many questions**' is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Corrected sentence:** *He was so curious that he raised many questions in the meeting. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Option 3: '**that he aroused many questions**' doesn't convey the same meaning as 'aroused' means to awaken or stimulate.
 
• Option 4: '**No substitution**' is not applicable as the underlined segment needs to be replaced.

questions.question:

Carolina opened a savings account to save __money for later.__
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**For a rainy day**" is an idiomatic expression that means saving money for unexpected future expenses or emergencies. (अप्रत्याशित भविष्य के खर्चों या आपात्कालीन स्थितियों के लिए धन की बचत करना)

 
 
• **For example-** *She always set aside money for a rainy day, just in case something unexpected happened.*
 
 
 
• "**Rainy day**" here symbolizes difficult times or unexpected situations.
 
• Just as rain can come unexpectedly and disrupt plans, financial emergencies can also arise suddenly.
 
• Saving money "**for a rainy day**" means putting money aside to be prepared for these unforeseen events.
 
• The use of this expression in the sentence implies that Carolina is being financially responsible and preparing for the future.
